item.title: [LU-20939] OST umount stuck in inode cache cleanup
item.description:
An unusually long umount duration was observed on the HDD OSTs during the maintenance window. After 25 minutes, the decision was made by the administrators to reboot the OSS.

They take one OSS crash:

crash> foreach 'umount' bt -s
 #0  __schedule at
 #1  schedule at
 #2  io_schedule at
 #3  bit_wait_io at
 #4  __wait_on_bit at
 #5  out_of_line_wait_on_bit at
 #6  ldiskfs_wait_block_bitmap at [ldiskfs]
 #7  ldiskfs_mb_init_cache at [ldiskfs]
 #8  ldiskfs_mb_load_buddy_gfp at [ldiskfs]
 #9  ldiskfs_discard_preallocations at [ldiskfs]
#10  ldiskfs_clear_inode at [ldiskfs]
#11  ldiskfs_evict_inode at [ldiskfs]
#12  evict at
#13  dispose_list at
#14  evict_inodes at
#15  generic_shutdown_super at
#16  kill_block_super at
#17  deactivate_locked_super at
#18  cleanup_mnt at
#19  osd_umount at [osd_ldiskfs]
#20  osd_device_fini at [osd_ldiskfs]
#21  class_cleanup at [obdclass]
#22  class_process_config at [obdclass]
#23  class_manual_cleanup at [obdclass]
#24  osd_obd_disconnect at [osd_ldiskfs]
#25  lustre_put_lsi at [obdclass]
#26  server_put_super at [obdclass]
#27  generic_shutdown_super at
#28  kill_anon_super at
#29  deactivate_locked_super at
#30  cleanup_mnt at
#31  task_work_run at
#32  exit_to_usermode_loop at
#33  do_syscall_64 at
#34  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe at

The OST device target was busy at 100% doing 4k IOs. The umount process seems stuck reading block bitmaps for freeing/clearing inode block preallocations:

crash> kmem -s | grep ldiskfs_prealloc
      104     312822    616902  15818     4k ldiskfs_prealloc_space 
crash> kmem -i
                 PAGES        TOTAL      PERCENTAGE
    TOTAL MEM  18157679      69.3 GB         ----
         FREE  3099014      11.8 GB   17% of TOTAL MEM
         USED  15058665      57.4 GB   82% of TOTAL MEM
       SHARED  4001901      15.3 GB   22% of TOTAL MEM
      BUFFERS  4976421        19 GB   27% of TOTAL MEM
       CACHED  6445517      24.6 GB   35% of TOTAL MEM
         SLAB   738982       2.8 GB    4% of TOTAL MEM

   TOTAL HUGE        0            0         ----
    HUGE FREE        0            0    0% of TOTAL HUGE

   TOTAL SWAP        0            0         ----
    SWAP USED        0            0    0% of TOTAL SWAP
    SWAP FREE        0            0    0% of TOTAL SWAP

 COMMIT LIMIT  9078839      34.6 GB         ----
    COMMITTED  1131056       4.3 GB   12% of TOTAL LIMIT

Hypothesis
The ldiskfs inodes still in kernel cache reference block preallocations using different ext4 groups distributed on all the volume surface. The group bitmaps does not seems to be in cache, so a read is needed (due to cache eviction?). This is causing random 4K IO to read all the bitmaps.

Here some preallocation information:

struct ldiskfs_sb_info {
  s_blocks_per_group = 32768,
  s_clusters_per_group = 32768,
  s_inodes_per_group = 128,
  s_itb_per_group = 16,
  s_gdb_count = 80112,
  s_desc_per_block = 64,
  s_groups_count = 5127168,

  s_stripe = 1024,
  s_mb_small_req = 1024,
  s_mb_large_req = 8192,
  s_mb_max_to_scan = 200,
  s_mb_min_to_scan = 10,
  s_mb_stats = 0,
  s_mb_order2_reqs = 8,
  s_mb_c1_blocks = 42001760250,
  s_mb_c2_blocks = 25201056150,
  s_mb_c3_blocks = 8400352050,
  s_mb_prealloc_table = 0xff12c8e1a9cd0c00,
  s_mb_group_prealloc = 4096,
  s_mb_max_inode_prealloc = 512,
  s_max_dir_size_kb = 0,
  s_warning_dir_size = 0,
  s_mb_last_group = 1885531,
  s_mb_last_start = 12288,
  s_mb_prefetch = 2048,
  s_mb_prefetch_limit = 8192,

The s_stripe = 1024 value appears to be a FS formatting error: the admin intended to define a stripe width of 1 MB, but the unit used is ext4 blocks, which results in 4 MB.
This means that the minimum allocation size is 4MB which not helping our issue.

# cat /proc/fs/ldiskfs/sdb/prealloc_table
1024 2048 4096

I have checked some inode preallocation, most of time, there is 1 preallocation per inode. These preallocation are usually at an offset of 1024-8192 blocks (non aligned write on small files).

Reproducer
I have been able to reproduce this type of behaviour on the OSTs after the maintenance window (~100000 prealloc entries in slab):

echo 2 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches

This took ~6s

On another OST:

echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches
echo 2 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches

This took ~15min.
item.environment:
2.18.8.ocean2 HDD OST server, 625.9 TB target (80-85% full)
RHEL 8.8
item.summary: OST umount stuck in inode cache cleanup

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

comments.comment: Hi eaujames, thanks for the detailed analysis. Do you plan on investigating further and push a tentative patch, or do you need an ldiskfs expert's eyes?
I have some ideas but I need to discuss about it

adilger, ablagodarenko and bzzz can you comment about this?

For now, I see 2 way to workaround this issue:

  • Do we need to keep ldiskfs inodes in kernel LRU cache after the osd objects died? If not, we can mark the inode to be dropped with the preallocation space: 
    static void iput_final(struct inode *inode) 
{
        struct super_block *sb = inode->i_sb;
        const struct super_operations *op = inode->i_sb->s_op;
        int drop;
                
        WARN_ON(inode->i_state & I_NEW);

        if (op->drop_inode)
                drop = op->drop_inode(inode);
        else
                drop = generic_drop_inode(inode);

        if (!drop &&
            !(inode->i_state & I_DONTCACHE) &&           <----
            (sb->s_flags & SB_ACTIVE)) {
                inode_add_lru(inode);
                spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock); 
                return;
        }

        if (!drop) {
                inode->i_state |= I_WILL_FREE;
                spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
                write_inode_now(inode, 1);
                spin_lock(&inode->i_lock);
                WARN_ON(inode->i_state & I_NEW);
                inode->i_state &= ~I_WILL_FREE;
        }

        inode->i_state |= I_FREEING;
        if (!list_empty(&inode->i_lru))
                inode_lru_list_del(inode);
        spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);

        evict(inode);
}

    We could set the I_DONTCACHE flag to force the inode to be freed .

    void d_mark_dontcache(struct inode *inode)
{       
        struct dentry *de;      
        
        spin_lock(&inode->i_lock);
        hlist_for_each_entry(de, &inode->i_dentry, d_u.d_alias) {
                spin_lock(&de->d_lock); 
                de->d_flags |= DCACHE_DONTCACHE;
                spin_unlock(&de->d_lock);
        }
        inode->i_state |= I_DONTCACHE;
        spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
}
EXPORT_SYMBOL(d_mark_dontcache);

    I know that delbaryg ran into issues benchmarking MDS with mdtest: the kswapd kernel threads couldn't keep up with the Lustre threads, and direct reclaim operations were slowing everything down. He had to tune the cache pressure and use tbf to make it work.

  • Dropping the per-inode preallocation space is not efficient on HDD: it causes random I/O across the entire surface of the target volume.
    Before unmounting the target, we can use ldiskfs_mb_discard_preallocations() to discard preallocations group by group. So we can take advantage of the volume readahead cache (even with flex_bg, the group bitmap are packed by 16).

if this is umount, then it's safe to discard preallocation and do not mark bitmaps at all:

void generic_shutdown_super(struct super_block *sb)
{
	const struct super_operations *sop = sb->s_op;

	if (sb->s_root) {
		shrink_dcache_for_umount(sb);
		sync_filesystem(sb);
		sb->s_flags &= ~SB_ACTIVE;

		cgroup_writeback_umount();

		/* Evict all inodes with zero refcount. */
		evict_inodes(sb);

so SB_ACTIVE has been cleared and we can check that in ldiskfs_discard_preallocations()

just checked and this code seems to pass simple tests:

--- ../head1/ldiskfs/mballoc.c	2026-10-02 17:15:07.088743878 +0300
+++ ldiskfs/mballoc.c	2026-10-13 19:47:09.496665241 +0300
@@ -5920,6 +5920,17 @@ repeat:
 	}
 	write_unlock(&ei->i_prealloc_lock);
 
+	if (!(sb->s_flags & SB_ACTIVE)) {
+		list_for_each_entry_safe(pa, tmp, &list, u.pa_tmp_list) {
+			ldiskfs_lock_group(sb, group);
+			list_del(&pa->pa_group_list);
+			ldiskfs_unlock_group(sb, group);
+			list_del(&pa->u.pa_tmp_list);
+			ldiskfs_mb_pa_free(pa);
+		}
+		return;
+	}
+
 	list_for_each_entry_safe(pa, tmp, &list, u.pa_tmp_list) {
 		BUG_ON(pa->pa_type != MB_INODE_PA);
 		group = ldiskfs_get_group_number(sb, pa->pa_pstart);

bzzz thanks, your fix seems fine.

I have misunderstood the code. I was thinking the preallocations was written on-disk bitmaps. But actually, these are written in buddy RAM "file" bitmaps. In our case, the buddy bitmap pages of the group get evicted, so it needs to be reconstructed: it get the on-disk bitmap copy and then re-register block preallocations on it (ext4_mb_generate_from_pa()). But here on umount, we don't care about updating the buddy bitmaps.

What do you think about dropping the ldiskfs_inode when an osd object is evicted from memory?
# By default the object cache is unlimited, so the kernel shrinker needs scan 2 times to free an ldiskfs_inode. 1 to free the object and 1 to free the ldiskfs inode (referenced by osd object).

  1. Keep the inode preallocation for unreferenced ldiskfs inode does not make sense. Ext4 cleans the preallocation when the file get released (last close). This have an overhead to reconstruct the buddy page. And this will slowly consume space: if there are no more spaces on the OST, ldiskfs needs to direclty free some preallocations to allocate new blocks.
    Actually, this would make sense to clear the inode preallocations when the osd_object is not referenced anymore (client LDLM locks get cancelled?).
